claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has higher configurational entropy than compositionally imbalanced CoCrFeMnNi variants.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys have enhanced structural stability at high temperature relative to non-equiatomic variants.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys have enhanced chemical stability at high temperature relative to non-equiatomic variants.
Higher configurational entropy raises the energy barrier for atomic diffusion or mixing.
Reduced atomic mobility and diffusion improve high-temperature microstructural stability.
The equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi starting nanoalloy is single phase.
Deliberately departing from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi ratios reduces configurational entropy.
Equiatomic and non-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys can be compared after identical isothermal annealing at approximately 950 °C under inert atmosphere.
Elemental distribution within the lattice can be used to assess atomic mixing and configurational disorder.
Chemical complexity and packing disorder in high-entropy alloys are associated with sluggish atomic diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion delays phase separation and chemical segregation in CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will retain a single-phase structure better than a non-equiatomic variant after identical annealing.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will retain a more uniform elemental distribution than a non-equiatomic variant after identical annealing.
Chemical segregation will progress more slowly in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi than in a non-equiatomic variant.
The non-equiatomic baseline will exhibit faster diffusion and earlier phase separation because of its lower configurational entropy.
The prediction is limited to annealing near 950 °C under inert atmosphere and before contamination or uncontrolled intermetallic precipitation becomes important.
Changing to a non-equiatomic composition can promote secondary phases or intermetallic formation independently of configurational entropy.
Failure of the equiatomic material to show improved single-phase retention and reduced segregation relative to the control would falsify the proposed mechanism.
